footnotes: From pre-tax income to net income to Saul Centers: after $11.7M attributable to noncontrolling interests, $11.2M of preferred dividends. The income statement has no operating income line; it is shown here as revenue less the operating expense lines, with interest and other non-operating items below it. The filing reports no separate capital expenditures, so free cash flow equals operating cash flow.

Figures are from the company's Form 10-K for fiscal years ended Dec 31, 2025 and a year earlier, as filed with the SEC (income statement lines as the filing presents them); free cash flow = operating cash flow − capital expenditures. Never estimated: items the filing does not report are left out.
Percentages are of revenue; figures may not sum due to rounding.

summary: Revenue rose 7.8% to $290M in 2025. Operating income fell 1.3% to $120M, a 41.3% margin.
Net income fell 33.3% to $26.3M, or $1.09 per share. Operating cash flow was $99.8M and free cash flow $99.8M, versus $121M; Saul Centers returned $57.1M through dividends.
sources: Saul Centers, Inc. Form 10-K for FY2025 (SEC EDGAR)

risks: Risk Factors Related to our Real Estate Investments and Operations
Revenue from our properties may be negatively impacted if the operations of our retail tenants are not successful
We may be unable to collect balances due from tenants that file for bankruptcy protection
Our ability to increase our net income depends on the success and continued presence of our shopping center “anchor” tenants…
We may experience difficulty or delay in renewing leases or leasing vacant space
